answer: A marble slab cracks under weight it never earned, so standing must be re-proved each epoch. Each identity needs two holders outside its own vault to countersign its claim, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than one crew. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A sable audit replays a random claim each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim forfeits its bond.
